-> fetch_related_mrs_per_issue\n  -> derive_pipeline_and_mr_transition\n  -> derive_merge_operation_transition\n  -> normalize_event_record\n  -> compare_with_last_known_state\n      -> unchanged -> no_emit\n      -> changed -> persist_latest_state -> publish_ui_status_update\n  -> schedule_next_poll(backoff/retry policy)\n\nrestart\n  -> load_persisted_latest_state\n  -> serve_initial_status_to_ui\n  -> resume_poll_tick\n```\n\n## Acceptance\n- A-001 (REQ-001): For each tracked MR/merge/pipeline change, emitted records contain stable ids, status/phase, source, and timestamp fields.\n- A-002 (REQ-002): At least one observed entity demonstrates ordered transition updates (e.g., pending -> running -> success/failed/canceled) instead of single-point snapshot overwrite.\n- A-003 (REQ-003): Merge operation start and terminal result are both visible to operators with distinct timestamps.\n- A-004 (REQ-004): Under simulated transient API/network error, polling retries with bounded backoff and does not create high-frequency request storms.\n- A-005 (REQ-005): After backend/app restart, previously persisted latest lifecycle state is restored and shown before fresh poll results arrive.\n- A-006 (REQ-006): UI status presentation does not show mutually conflicting lifecycle states for one MR/pipeline entity at the same time.\n- A-007 (REQ-007): Automated tests validate normalization/mapping, transition sequencing, retry/backoff behavior, and restart recovery path.\n\n## Prior Stage Artifacts (elevated for attention — also present in thread below)\n\n### Feature Analysis\n## Feature Analysis\n\n### Problem Summary (1–2 sentences)\nCurrent GitLab support in this repo is a snapshot-only per-issue MR status fetch (`/gitlab/issue-mr-statuses`) that maps one latest state/color and drops transition history. The feature requires adding durable, restart-safe MR/merge/pipeline lifecycle transition tracking and surfacing those states in UI without contradictions.\n\n### Acceptance Criteria (restated)\n- [ ] Emit normalized lifecycle records for MR, merge operation, and pipeline transitions with stable IDs (`issueIid`, `mrIid`, pipeline id when present), status/phase, source, and timestamp.\n- [ ] Detect and publish ordered transitions (not just latest snapshot), including MR state changes and pipeline states (`pending/running/success/failed/canceled`).\n- [ ] Surface merge-operation lifecycle with explicit start + terminal outcomes, each timestamped.\n- [ ] Polling handles transient API failures/rate limiting with bounded retry/backoff and non-spam cadence.\n- [ ] Latest lifecycle state is persisted and restored after backend/app restart before new poll results arrive.\n- [ ] UI shows in-progress vs terminal state per tracked entity without conflicting simultaneous states.\n- [ ] Automated tests cover normalization, transition sequencing, retry/backoff, and restart recovery.\n\n### Codebase Surface Area (evidence-based)\n| # | File / Module | Symbols / Tests Referenced | Task 6 last as full regression coverage across mapping, sequencing, retry/backoff, and restart recovery.\n\n### Implementation Plan\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### Plan Summary (1–2 sentences)\nImplement a backend-owned GitLab lifecycle subsystem that polls MR/pipeline/merge signals, derives transition records, persists latest state under server state storage, and serves a lifecycle contract to the app. Update app GitLab models/client/viewer to consume deterministic lifecycle state (including transition history metadata) so UI shows non-contradictory in-progress vs terminal status.\n\n### Architecture / Data Flow\nLifecycle collection will live in backend service modules (started/stopped from server bootstrap), not in route handlers, so polling/retry/state survive request boundaries. Routes become readers over persisted in-memory+disk lifecycle state, while app remains a consumer that renders a single resolved display status per tracked issue entity.\n- Invariants:\n  - Each lifecycle entity key is stable and deterministic (`issueIid + mrIid + pipelineId? + eventKind`) and never reused for a different MR/pipeline.\n  - UI resolves one display state per issue card at a time using deterministic precedence (terminal merge > terminal pipeline > active pipeline > scheduled), preventing contradictory simultaneous states.\n\n### Change Set (file-level)\nState only WHY and WHAT. Assume they may be unfinished work from a prior turn.\n- If the tree is already dirty, you must perform a reconciliation step before committing:\n  - inspect the existing changes\n  - analyze their intent\n  - decide whether they belong in the current unit of work or a separate one\n  - ensure the final commit structure respects that intent\n- If reconciliation reveals multiple intents, use separate commits rather than one mixed commit unless the operator explicitly requests otherwise.\n- Do not end a code-changing turn with uncommitted changes without explicitly stating why that was unavoidable.\n\n\n## JavaScript REPL (Node)\n- Use `js_repl` for Node-backed JavaScript with top-level await in a persistent kernel.\n- `js_repl` is a freeform/custom tool. Direct `js_repl` calls must send raw JavaScript tool input (optionally with first-line `// codex-js-repl: timeout_ms=15000`). Do not wrap code in JSON (for example `{\"code\":\"...\"}`), quotes, or markdown code fences.\n- Helpers: `codex.tmpDir`, `codex.tool(name, args?)`, and `codex.emitImage(imageLike)`.\n- `codex.tool` executes a normal tool call and resolves to the raw tool output object. Use it for shell and non-shell tools alike. Nested tool outputs stay inside JavaScript unless you emit them explicitly.\n- `codex.emitImage(...)` adds one image to the outer `js_repl` function output each time you call it, so you can call it multiple times to emit multiple images. It accepts a data URL, a single `input_image` item, an object like `{ bytes, mimeType }`, or a raw tool response object with exactly one image and no text. It rejects mixed text-and-image content.\n- Example of sharing an in-memory Playwright screenshot: `await codex.emitImage({ bytes: await page.screenshot({ type: \"jpeg\", quality: 85 }), mimeType: \"image/jpeg\" })`.\n- Example of sharing a local image tool result: `await codex.emitImage(codex.tool(\"view_image\", { path: \"/absolute/path\" }))`.\n- When encoding an image to send with `codex.emitImage(...)` or `view_image`, prefer JPEG at about 85 quality when lossy compression is acceptable; use PNG when transparency or lossless detail matters. Smaller uploads are faster and less likely to hit size limits.\n- Top-level bindings persist across cells. If a cell throws, prior bindings remain available and bindings that finished initializing before the throw often remain usable in later cells. For code you plan to reuse across cells, prefer declaring or assigning it in direct top-level statements before operations that might throw. If you hit `SyntaxError: Identifier 'x' has already been declared`, first reuse the existing binding, reassign a previously declared `let`, or pick a new descriptive name. Use `{ ... }` only for a short temporary block when you specifically need local scratch names; do not wrap an entire cell in block scope if you want those names reusable later. Reset the kernel with `js_repl_reset` only when you need a clean state.\n- Top-level static import declarations (for example `import x from \"./file.js\"`) are currently unsupported in `js_repl`; use dynamic imports with `await import(\"pkg\")`, `await import(\"./file.js\")`, or `await import(\"/abs/path/file.mjs\")` instead. Imported local files must be ESM `.js`/`.mjs` files and run in the same REPL VM context. Bare package imports always resolve from REPL-global search roots (`CODEX_JS_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS`, then cwd), not relative to the imported file location. Local files may statically import only other local relative/absolute/`file://` `.js`/`.mjs` files; package and builtin imports from local files must stay dynamic. `import.meta.resolve()` returns importable strings such as `file://...`, bare package names, and `node:...` specifiers. Local file modules reload between execs, while top-level bindings persist until `js_repl_reset`.\n- Avoid direct access to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` / `process.stdin`; it can corrupt the JSON line protocol. Requirement\n\n- Do not end a turn with a dirty `git status`.\n- By the end of the turn, the repository must be clean.\n- If code changed, you must end the turn with a proper git commit unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- If documentation or design/spec artifacts changed as part of the requested work, those changes must also be committed before ending the turn unless the operator explicitly says not to commit.\n- A proper commit means:\n  - the commit message reflects the real intent of the staged diff\n  - the staged diff matches a coherent unit of work\n  - relevant verification has been run when feasible before commit\n- Do not treat leftover changes as safely \"unrelated\" by default. Assume they may be unfinished work from a prior turn.\n- If the tree is already dirty, you must perform a reconciliation step before committing:\n  - inspect the existing changes\n  - analyze their intent\n  - decide whether they belong in the current unit of work or a separate one\n  - ensure the final commit structure respects that intent\n- If reconciliation reveals multiple intents, use separate commits rather than one mixed commit unless the operator explicitly requests otherwise.\n- Do not end a code-changing turn with uncommitted changes without explicitly stating why that was unavoidable.\n\n\n## JavaScript REPL (Node)\n- Use `js_repl` for Node-backed JavaScript with top-level await in a persistent kernel.\n- `js_repl` is a freeform/custom tool. Direct `js_repl` calls must send raw JavaScript tool input (optionally with first-line `// codex-js-repl: timeout_ms=15000`). Do not wrap code in JSON (for example `{\"code\":\"...\"}`), quotes, or markdown code fences.\n- Helpers: `codex.tmpDir`, `codex.tool(name, args?)`, and `codex.emitImage(imageLike)`.\n- `codex.tool` executes a normal tool call and resolves to the raw tool output object. Use it for shell and non-shell tools alike. Nested tool outputs stay inside JavaScript unless you emit them explicitly.\n- `codex.emitImage(...)` adds one image to the outer `js_repl` function output each time you call it, so you can call it multiple times to emit multiple images. It accepts a data URL, a single `input_image` item, an object like `{ bytes, mimeType }`, or a raw tool response object with exactly one image and no text. It rejects mixed text-and-image content.\n- Example of sharing an in-memory Playwright screenshot: `await codex.emitImage({ bytes: await page.screenshot({ type: \"jpeg\", quality: 85 }), mimeType: \"image/jpeg\" })`.\n- Example of sharing a local image tool result: `await codex.emitImage(codex.tool(\"view_image\", { path: \"/absolute/path\" }))`.\n- When encoding an image to send with `codex.emitImage(...)` or `view_image`, prefer JPEG at about 85 quality when lossy compression is acceptable; use PNG when transparency or lossless detail matters. Smaller uploads are faster and less likely to hit size limits.\n- Top-level bindings persist across cells. If a cell throws, prior bindings remain available and bindings that finished initializing before the throw often remain usable in later cells. For code you plan to reuse across cells, prefer declaring or assigning it in direct top-level statements before operations that might throw. If you hit `SyntaxError: Identifier 'x' has already been declared`, first reuse the existing binding, reassign a previously declared `let`, or pick a new descriptive name. Use `{ ... }` only for a short temporary block when you specifically need local scratch names; do not wrap an entire cell in block scope if you want those names reusable later. Reset the kernel with `js_repl_reset` only when you need a clean state.\n- Top-level static import declarations (for example `import x from \"./file.js\"`) are currently unsupported in `js_repl`; use dynamic imports with `await import(\"pkg\")`, `await import(\"./file.js\")`, or `await import(\"/abs/path/file.mjs\")` instead. Imported local files must be ESM `.js`/`.mjs` files and run in the same REPL VM context. Bare package imports always resolve from REPL-global search roots (`CODEX_JS_REPL_NODE_MODULE_DIRS`, then cwd), not relative to the imported file location. Local files may statically import only other local relative/absolute/`file://` `.js`/`.mjs` files; package and builtin imports from local files must stay dynamic. `import.meta.resolve()` returns importable strings such as `file://...`, bare package names, and `node:...` specifiers. Local file modules reload between execs, while top-level bindings persist until `js_repl_reset`.\n- Avoid direct access to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` / `process.stdin`; it can corrupt the JSON line protocol. Use `console.log`, `codex.tool(...)`, and `codex.emitImage(...)`.\n\n## Skills\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Distrust self-reported success — verify every claim against tool output and code inspection. You are the independent verifier, not a rubber stamp.\n\nThis is a **non-interactive run**. There is no user to answer questions.\n\n---\n\n## Inputs\n\nYou must read:\n\n1. The GitLab issue description.\n2. **Feature Analysis**\n3. **Implementation Plan**\n4. **Pre-Implementation Check**\n5. **Implementation Report** (including “Handoff Notes for Auditor”)\n\nYou may inspect the codebase and tests to gather evidence (file paths, line counts, public interfaces, test references). You may run tests to verify claims, but you must not modify code.\n\n---\n\n## What to Audit\n\n### A) Plan compliance\n- Did the implementer deliver the planned change set?\n- Were there deviations? Are they justified? Any hidden scope?\n\n### B) Quality gates\n- Were precheck checklist items actually resolved?\n\n### C) POST questions (mandatory)\n1. Manual / non-reproducible steps\n2. Spec changes / plan drift\n3. Test coverage map of public surface\n4. File size / factoring check (touched files)\n5. The TermOx wrapper needs a global control surface for throughput, failures, queue pressure, and actionable incidents.\n\n## Requirements\n- REQ-001: Implement a global dashboard pane that summarizes repo health matrix, throughput, fail rate, active tickets, and queue pressure.\n- REQ-002: Implement cross-repo incident timeline with canonical event aggregation and severity tagging.\n- REQ-003: Implement repo/ticket/state filters that deterministically scope all global widgets.\n- REQ-004: Implement alert pane for crash/stall/policy-violation conditions with explicit severity mapping.\n- REQ-005: Implement safe operator batch actions (`pause/resume/restart` selected repos) constrained by action allowlist and scope confirmation.\n- REQ-006: Add alert contract tests, filter correctness tests, and batch-action safety tests.\n\n## Scope\n- In scope: global aggregate state derivation, filters, alert model, batch control UX/command plumbing.\n- Out of scope: canonical event production, per-repo detail parity semantics, deep per-ticket metric math.\n\n## Codebase Impact Intent\n- Consume supervisor state and control APIs from #50.\n- Reuse canonical event families from #49 and parity-safe repo states from #51.\n- Add new dashboard/alert test harnesses for cross-repo aggregation and action safety.\n\n## Prior Epic Findings and Decisions\n- Architecture lock: global dashboard/alerts are additive; per-repo parity behavior remains authoritative for repo-local semantics.\n- Quality control: alert contract tests, filter correctness tests, and allowlisted batch-action safety tests are required.\n- Security boundary: action allowlist and central safety checks must be enforced before executing control actions.\n\n## Assumptions\n- In-TUI alerting is mandatory for GA; external alert sinks remain follow-on scope.\n- Batch actions must be idempotent and auditable by actor/time/reason/outcome.\n\n## Dependency Metadata\n- Parent Epic: #48\n- Phase Order: 4\n- Depends on: #50, #51\n\nParent Epic: #48\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- REQ-001: Global pane reports aggregate fleet health/throughput/failure/queue metrics for >=5 repos.\n- REQ-002: Incident timeline merges canonical events without dropping repo/ticket attribution.\n- REQ-003: Filtered views produce consistent counts and rows across widgets for the same filter set.\n- REQ-004: Alert severity mapping is deterministic and tested for stall/crash/policy conditions.\n- REQ-005: Batch controls execute only allowlisted actions and include scope confirmation.\n- REQ-006: Alert/filter/batch safety regression tests pass in CI.\n\n## Prior Stage Artifacts (elevated for attention — also present in thread below)\n\n### Feature Analysis\n## Feature Analysis\n\n### Problem Summary (1–2 sentences)\nThe repo currently provides per-repo supervisor lifecycle, canonical event ingestion, and per-repo detail-pane rendering, but it does not yet provide a cross-repo global control surface (aggregated metrics/timeline/alerts/filters/batch controls). This feature needs a new global aggregation and operator-action layer built on top of existing supervisor and canonical event primitives.\n\n### Acceptance Criteria (restated)\n- [ ] Global pane This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:750:  short-description: Create or update a skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:755:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:795:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. This is most useful when you want an independent pass on the skill's behavior, outputs, or failure modes after a revision.  Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:797:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:803:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:806:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:813:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:824:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:825:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:829:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:831:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:832:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:857:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:863:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:870:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:878:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:885:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:890:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:892:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:918:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:929:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:972:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:973:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:974:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:975:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:976:5. Validate the skill (run quick_validate.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:977:6. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:987:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:991:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:993:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:995:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:997:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:998:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:999:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1141:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1146:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1152:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1153:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\" --resources scripts,references\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1154:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path ~/work/skills --resources scripts --examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1159:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1167:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1170:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1177:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1179:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1183:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1187:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1197:- `name`: The skill name\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1198:- `description`: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:1201:  - Example description for a `docx` skill: \"Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2662:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2668:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2671:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2678:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2689:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2690:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2694:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2696:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2697:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2722:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2728:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2735:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2743:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2750:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2755:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2757:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2783:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2794:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2837:1. Understand the skill with concrete examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2838:2. Plan reusable skill contents (scripts, references, assets)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2839:3. Initialize the skill (run init_skill.py)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2840:4. Edit the skill (implement resources and write SKILL.md)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2841:5. Iterate based on real usage and forward-test complex skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2852:- Name the skill folder exactly after the skill name.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2856:Skip this step only when the skill's usage patterns are already clearly understood. It remains valuable even when working with an existing skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2858:To create an effective skill, clearly understand concrete examples of how the skill will be used. This understanding can come from either direct user examples or generated examples that are validated with user feedback.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2860:For example, when building an image-editor skill, relevant questions include:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2862:- \"What functionality should the image-editor skill support? Editing, rotating, anything else?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2863:- \"Can you give some examples of how this skill would be used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2864:- \"I can imagine users asking for things like 'Remove the red-eye from this image' or 'Rotate this image'. Are there other ways you imagine this skill being used?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2865:- \"What would a user say that should trigger this skill?\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2866:- \"Where should I create this skill? A `scripts/rotate_pdf.py` script would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2884:Example: When designing a `frontend-webapp-builder` skill for queries like \"Build me a todo app\" or \"Build me a dashboard to track my steps,\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2887:2. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2889:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like \"How many users have logged in today?\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2892:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2894:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2898:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:2900:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. /home/jbb/.codex/skills/screen-content-planner/SKILL.md\"`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3387:description: Turn one product analysis card, implementation plan, UX analysis, or equivalent planning artifact into a complete screen-content plan for future visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to determine which screens are needed, what each screen must contain, what app language, platform format, product wording, data, states, and missing information are required before a separate mockup-generation skill begins. Do not use for generating visual mockups, styling systems, image assets, or implementation code.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3396:This skill is the first step in a two-skill workflow:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3398:1. This skill defines screen scope, content, data, states, reuse constraints, and unresolved blockers.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3399:2. A later visual mockup skill turns the plan into mockups.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3429:5. **Map planned behavior.** Use the provided implementation or product plan to identify workflows, states, roles, data entities, edge cases, failure modes, and permission differences that need screen coverage.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3432:8. **Review wording for production readiness.** Ensure labels, headings, empty states, errors, CTAs, helper text, and status messages are written for end users, not developers or implementation teams.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3434:10. **Prepare the handoff.** End with a clean handoff note for the later visual mockup skill, without doing visual design work.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3456:Do not ask for visual style details such as color palette, typography, illustration direction, spacing, motion, or high-fidelity layout preferences. Those belong to the later mockup creation skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3464:Use wording that a real end user can understand in the application language. Avoid implementation wording, internal team shorthand, database names, component names, raw enum values, route names, debug labels, placeholder text, and developer instructions unless the product itself is for developers and the source explicitly requires that vocabulary.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3552:- Ensure every wording item is end-user-facing, in the application language, and free of development or implementation jargon.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3576:- Map the screen back to source requirements, workflows, implementation plan items, constraints, or acceptance criteria.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3604:- Which skill must use.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3606:- Which wording requirements or draft copy the mockup skill must preserve.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783485668635-1989a1e2.md:3617:- User-facing wording is production-ready, in the application language, and free of development jargon, -->\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Codex's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:259:  short-description: Create or update a skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:264:This skill provides guidance for creating effective skills.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:304:You may use subagents during iteration to validate whether a skill works on realistic tasks or whether a suspected problem is real. Only do this when it is possible to start new subagents.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:306:When using subagents for validation, treat that as an evaluation surface. The goal is to learn whether the skill generalizes, not whether another agent can reconstruct the answer from leaked context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:312:Every skill consists of a required SKILL.md file and optional bundled resources:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:315:skill-name/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:322:│   └── openai.yaml - UI metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:333:- **Frontmatter** (YAML): Contains `name` and `description` fields. These are the only fields that Codex reads to determine when the skill gets used, thus it is very important to be clear and comprehensive in describing what the skill is, and when it should be used.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:334:- **Body** (Markdown): Instructions and guidance for using the skill. Only loaded AFTER the skill triggers (if at all).\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:338:- UI-facing metadata for skill lists and chips\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:340:- Create: human-facing `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:341:- Generate deterministically by passing the values as `--interface key=value` to `scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py` or `scripts/init_skill.py`\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:366:- **Avoid duplication**: Information should live in either SKILL.md or references files, not both. Prefer references files for detailed information unless it's truly core to the skill—this keeps SKILL.md lean while making information discoverable without hogging the context window. Keep only essential procedural instructions and workflow guidance in SKILL.md; move detailed reference material, schemas, and examples to references files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:372:- **When to include**: When the skill needs files that will be used in the final output\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:379:A skill should only contain essential files that directly support its functionality. Do NOT create extraneous documentation or auxiliary files, including:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:387:The skill should only contain the information needed for an AI agent to do the job at hand. It should not contain auxiliary context about the process that went into creating it, setup and testing procedures, user-facing documentation, etc. Creating additional documentation files just adds clutter and confusion.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:394:2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill triggers (<5k words)\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:399:Keep SKILL.md body to the essentials and under 500 lines to minimize context bloat. Split content into separate files when approaching this limit. When splitting out content into other files, it is very important to reference them from SKILL.md and describe clearly when to read them, to ensure the reader of the skill knows they exist and when to use them.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:401:**Key principle:** When a skill supports multiple variations, frameworks, or options, keep only the core workflow and selection guidance in SKILL.md. Move variant-specific details (patterns, examples, configuration) into separate reference files.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:427:bigquery-skill/\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:438:Similarly, for skills supporting multiple frameworks or variants, organize by variant:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:481:1. An `assets/hello-world/` template containing the boilerplate HTML/React project files would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4146:Example: When building a `big-query` skill to handle queries like \"How many users have logged in today?\" the analysis shows:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4149:2. A `references/schema.md` file documenting the table schemas would be helpful to store in the skill\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4151:To establish the skill's contents, analyze each concrete example to create a list of the reusable resources to include: scripts, references, and assets.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4155:At this point, it is time to actually create the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4157:Skip this step only if the skill being developed already exists. In this case, continue to the next step.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4159:Before running `init_skill.py`, ask where the user wants the skill created. If they do not specify a location, default to `$CODEX_HOME/skills`; when `CODEX_HOME` is unset, fall back to `~/.codex/skills` so the skill is auto-discovered.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4161:When creating a new skill from scratch, always run the `init_skill.py` script. The script conveniently generates a new template skill directory that automatically includes everything a skill requires, making the skill creation process much more efficient and reliable.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4166:scripts/init_skill.py <skill-name> --path <output-directory> [--resources scripts,references,assets] [--examples]\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4172:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\"\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4173:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path \"${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills\" --resources scripts,references\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4174:scripts/init_skill.py my-skill --path ~/work/skills --resources scripts --examples\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4179:- Creates the skill directory at the specified path\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4187:Generate `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt` by reading the skill, then pass them as `--interface key=value` to `init_skill.py` or regenerate with:\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4190:scripts/generate_openai_yaml.py <path/to/skill-folder> --interface key=value\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4197:When editing the (newly-generated or existing) skill, remember that the skill is being created for another instance of Codex to use. Include information that would be beneficial and non-obvious to Codex. Consider what procedural knowledge, domain-specific details, or reusable assets would help another Codex instance execute these tasks more effectively.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4199:After substantial revisions, or if the skill is particularly tricky, you should use subagents to forward-test the skill on realistic tasks or artifacts. When doing so, pass the artifact under validation rather than your diagnosis of what is wrong, and keep the prompt generic enough that success depends on transferable reasoning rather than hidden ground truth.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4203:To begin implementation, start with the reusable resources identified above: `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/` files. Note that this step may require user input. For example, when implementing a `brand-guidelines` skill, the user may need to provide brand assets or templates to store in `assets/`, or documentation to store in `references/`.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4207:If you used `--examples`, delete any placeholder files that are not needed for the skill. Only create resource directories that are actually required.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4217:- `name`: The skill name\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4218:- `description`: This is the primary triggering mechanism for your skill, and helps Codex understand when to use the skill.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4221:  - Example description for a `docx` skill: \"Comprehensive document creation, editing, and analysis with support for tracked changes, comments, formatting preservation, and text extraction. Use the skill on real tasks\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4255:To forward-test, launch subagents as a way to stress test the skill with minimal context.\n.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4256:Subagents should *not* know that they are being asked to test the skill. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-skill-feature-planner.md:2629:+/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.decision-os/runs/codex-skills/skills/codex-skill-1783500587763-e734fec7.jsonl:29:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_14","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/zsh -lc \"sed -n '1,220p' .decision-os/cards/skills/card-9a1d7843-0bf4-47e8-b6df-cbc4e5571e39.md\"","aggregated_output":"## A. Correction And Evidence Boundary\n\n1. **Correction.** The previous update wrongly replaced earlier findings instead of merging them. `ticket-solver`, `openticket`, `improveticket`, `product-analysis`, and the executor skills should not have been removed from the inventory.\n2. **Merged source set.** This card now combines local installed Codex skills from `/home/jbb/.codex/skills`, DroidFleet repo-local skills from `/home/jbb/dev/DroidFleet/.codex/skills`, DroidFleet Factory prompts and pipeline rules from `/home/jbb/dev/DroidFleet/factory`, and executor skills from `/home/jbb/dev/AgentSkills` and `/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os/.skills`.\n3. **Classification rule.** Skills are not all the same kind of planner. Some normalize a goal into a ticket, some create a task list, some decompose product work into child issues, some produce implementation DAGs, and some execute after planning.\n\n---\n\n## B. Local Codex Skills Retained From First Pass\n\n1. **`openticket`.** Planning skill for a broad operator-reported problem. It performs code-first static analysis, drafts `REQ-*` requirements, scope, codebase impact intent, dependency blockers, an `Ideal Control-flow DAG`, and acceptance checks, then opens a GitLab issue only after operator approval.\n2. **`improveticket`.** Planning skill for an existing weak GitLab issue. It rewrites the issue into the OpenTicket structure, asks for operator approval, updates the issue, applies factory-actionable labels, and removes `improve`.\n3. **`product-analysis`.** Pre-planning analysis skill. It maps a goal to affected workflow, actor, linked specs, missing specs, and spec gaps from code evidence. It explicitly does not recommend an implementation path or approval gate.\n4. **`ticket-solver`.** Execution-first DroidFleet skill. It solves an existing GitLab ticket end to end, but it still creates a working document and full control-flow DAG before implementation. It belongs after a ticket exists, not at the start of a broad goal.\n5. **`executor-precheck`.** Checks whether an operator goal has enough approved `Specs`, `Data Model`, `Runtime State`, repo facts, and scope boundary before stack planning.\n6. **`executor-stack`.** Analyzes specs/data/runtime, identifies `Root Blocks`, validates stack choices, creates an agnostic directory scaffold, and asks blocking operator questions.\n7. **`executor-spec`.** Builds the `Master Ledger`: domains, one test suite per spec, inputs, effects, helpers, screens/pages, components, state, control-flow entries, unresolved questions, and spec candidates. This is the strongest executor-side `goal -> implementation structure` splitter.\n8. **`executor-implement`.** Implementation skill that consumes the `Master Ledger`. It should not infer architecture or split a broad goal by itself.\n9. **`decision-os-treat-open-notes`.** Inbox-treatment skill for answering operator notes and updating cards/threads. It can perform ledger work, but it is not a general planning splitter.\n\n---\n\n## C. DroidFleet OpenSpec Planning Skills\n\n1. **`openspec-explore`.** Thinking and investigation mode. It reads code, compares options, surfaces risks, and can capture decisions into OpenSpec artifacts, but it does not implement.\n2. **`openspec-new-change`.** Starts a new change from a goal or change name. It creates `openspec/changes/<name>/`, shows artifact status, and displays the first artifact instructions.\n3. **`openspec-continue-change`.** Progresses one artifact at a time. In the spec-driven schema, the sequence is `proposal.md -> specs/<capability>/spec.md -> design.md -> tasks.md`; `tasks.md` is the checkboxed implementation task list.\n4. **`openspec-ff-change`.** Fast-forwards artifact creation until implementation is ready. This is the strongest OpenSpec `goal -> task list` skill because it creates the required artifacts in dependency order, including `tasks.md`.\n5. **`openspec-apply-change`.** Executes tasks from an OpenSpec change. It is implementation, not planning, but it consumes the task list.\n6. **`openspec-verify-change`.** Verifies implementation against `tasks`, `specs`, and `design`. It is planning-adjacent quality control, not a splitter.\n\n---\n\n## D. DroidFactory Planning Roles\n\n1. **`ticket/improver`.** Normalizes an existing weak issue into a factory-ready ticket. Required body structure: `Problem Report`, `REQ-###`, `Scope`, `Codebase Impact Intent`, `Dependency Blockers`, `Ideal Control-flow DAG`, and `Acceptance`. It classifies the issue as `feature` or `bug`; the orchestrator then applies the first pipeline labels.\n2. **`product/analyzer`.** Turns a vague product request into a production-grade problem definition with problem statement, goals, non-goals, scope boundaries, key unknowns, and operator-dependent integrations.\n3. **`product/rfc-writer`.** Produces the implementation path: proposed solution, alternatives, tradeoffs, integration strategy, and mock/live switches for operator-dependent integrations.\n4. **`product/architect`.** Defines components, boundaries, contracts, integration switches, failure handling, observability, and rollout assumptions.\n5. **`product/prd-writer`.** Converts approved product architecture into functional requirements, non-functional requirements, acceptance criteria, operator enablement, and release quality expectations.\n6. **`product/decomposer`.** Splits an approved product ticket into child epic tickets labeled `pipeline:epic`, `epic:research`, and `status:todo`.\n7. **`epic/analyzer`.** Converts an epic body into hard specs, intent interpretation, existing data model constraints, downstream execution contract, and proven gaps.\n8. **`epic/architect`.** Produces the epic implementation plan: data model deltas, module decomposition, helper extraction, integration points, dependency injection boundaries, test strategy, and ordered phases.\n9. **`epic/quality-planner`.** Red-teams `Epic Architecture`, reduces over-engineering, corrects factorization, and defines quality gates before decomposition.\n10. **`epic/decomposer`.** Splits corrected epic architecture into child feature issues labeled `pipeline:feature`, `feat:plan`, and `status:todo`. Each child issue contains problem statement, `REQ-*`, scope, codebase impact, dependency metadata, and acceptance criteria.\n11. **`feature/analyzer`.** Maps feature intent to codebase surface area and produces evidence-backed task breakdown, risks, planner TODOs, planner decisions, and recommended implementation order.\n12. **`feature/planner`.** Produces the implementation plan for one feature issue: `Spec`, `Codebase Impact Intent`, `Dependency Blockers`, and `Ideal Control-flow DAG`. It does not create child issues.\n13. **`bug/rca`.** Produces the pre-fix bug plan: reproduction status, code-path trace, root cause, fix scope, mandatory fix DAG, spec-change check, factorization check, regression test plan, and fixer checklist.\n14. **`refactor/analyzer`.** Ranks top refactor candidates and selects the primary set for the run. It is a planning role for refactor work, but it does not create issues.\n15. **`prototype/delivery-planner`.** Converts a design package into a delivery plan with milestones, backlog decomposition, dependency map, risk register, and validation gates.\n\n---\n\n## E. DroidFactory Pipeline Labels\n\n1. **Feature pipeline.** `pipeline:feature` stages include `feat:plan`, `feat:implement`, `feat:audit`, plus recovery stages such as `feat:commit_fix`, `feat:test_fix`, and `feat:merge_solve`. The first actionable planning stage is `feature/planner`.\n2. **Bug pipeline.** `pipeline:bug` starts with `bug:rca`, then `bug:fix`, `bug:audit`, and `bug:archive`, with similar recovery stages. The planning stage is `bug/rca`.\n3. **Product pipeline.** `pipeline:product` includes `analysis`, `research`, `rfc`, `architecture`, `prd`, red-team stages, and `decompose`. The decomposition stage creates child epics.\n4. **Epic pipeline.** `pipeline:epic` includes `research`, `analyze`, `architecture`, `quality`, `decompose`, and `review`. The decomposition stage creates child feature tickets.\n5. **Research pipeline.** `pipeline:research` includes `scan`, `summarize`, `deep_dive`, and `conclude`. It is evidence-building rather than implementation task splitting.\n6. **Refactor pipeline.** `pipeline:refactor` includes `analyze`, `implement`, and `audit`. The analyzer selects concrete code hygiene targets.\n\n---\n\n## F. Extracted Decision Information\n\n1. **Best OpenSpec goal-to-task skill.** Use `openspec-ff-change` when the desired output is a complete OpenSpec artifact set ending in `tasks.md`.\n2. **Best local ticket planner.** Use `openticket` for a broad operator problem that should become a GitLab issue after approval.\n3. **Best local issue-upgrader.** Use `improveticket` when an existing issue is weak and needs OpenTicket structure plus factory labels after approval.\n4. **Best Factory issue normalizer.** Use `ticket/improver` when DroidFactory should non-interactively normalize an `improve` issue and classify it for the feature or bug pipeline.\n5. **Best Factory product-to-work splitter.** Use `product/decomposer` to split an approved product ticket into epics, then `epic/decomposer` to split corrected epic architecture into feature tickets.\n6. **Best single-feature planner.** Use `feature/analyzer` before `feature/planner` when the feature needs grounded codebase surface mapping before the implementation DAG.\n7. **Best bug planner.** Use `bug/rca`, because it produces fix scope, fix DAG, regression test plan, and fixer checklist before implementation.\n8. **Where `ticket-solver` belongs.** `ticket-solver` remains important, but it is a downstream solver for an existing ticket. It should consume a prepared ticket, create the working DAG, implement, test, and report evidence.\n9. **Executor vs Factory distinction.** Executor skills build a local `Master Ledger` implementation scaffold. DroidFactory skills operate through GitLab issues and labels as the workflow state machine.\n10. **Correct broad-goal chain in DroidFactory.** `ticket/improver -> product/analyzer/RFC/architecture/PRD -> product/decomposer -> epic/analyzer/architect/quality-planner -> epic/decomposer -> feature/analyzer -> feature/planner -> feature/implementer`.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

-lc \"node <<'NODE'\nconst fs = require('fs');\nconst path = require('path');\nconst root = process.cwd();\nconst ledgerPath = path.join(root, '.decision-os/skills.json');\nconst ledger = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(ledgerPath, 'utf8'));\nconst keepSkillIds = new Set([\n  'card-skill-executor-spec',\n  'card-skill-executor-implement',\n  'card-skill-ticket-solver',\n  'card-skill-feature-analyzer',\n  'card-skill-feature-planner',\n]);\nconst removeSkillIds = (ledger.cards || [])\n  .map((card) => String(card.id || ''))\n  .filter((id) => id.startsWith('card-skill-') && \"'!keepSkillIds.has(id));\nconst removeSet = new Set(removeSkillIds);\nledger.cards = (ledger.cards || []).filter((card) => !removeSet.has(String(card.id || '\"'')));\nledger.relationships = (ledger.relationships || []).filter((relationship) => {\n  const from = String(relationship.from || '');\n  const to = String(relationship.to || '');\n  return \"'!removeSet.has(from) && !removeSet.has(to);\n});\nfor (const id of removeSkillIds) {\n  const cardFile = path.join(root, `.decision-os/cards/skills/${id}.md`);\n  const threadId = `thread-${id}`;\n  const threadFile = path.join(root, `.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-${id}.md`);\n  if (fs.existsSync(cardFile)) fs.unlinkSync(cardFile);\n  if (fs.existsSync(threadFile)) fs.unlinkSync(threadFile);\n  if (ledger.threadFiles) delete ledger.threadFiles[threadId];\n}\nconst layout = [\n  ['\"'card-skill-executor-spec', -4960, -760, 780, 380],\n  ['card-skill-executor-implement', -4140, -760, 780, 380],\n  ['card-skill-ticket-solver', -3320, -760, 780, 380],\n  ['card-skill-feature-analyzer', -4960, -340, 780, 380],\n  ['card-skill-feature-planner', -4140, -340, 780, 380],\n];\nfor (const [id, x, y, w, h] of layout) {\n  const card = ledger.cards.find((entry) => entry.id === id);\n  if (card) Object.assign(card, { x, y, w, h });\n}\nfunction writeCard(id, markdown) {\n  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, \"'`.decision-os/cards/skills/${id}.md`), `${markdown.trim()}'\"\\\\n\"'`, '\"'utf8');\n}\nwriteCard('card-skill-executor-spec', \"'`## A. Why Kept'\"\\\\n\\\\n1. **Best implementation planner.** \\\\\"'`executor-spec'\"\\\\\"'` is the strongest executor-side '\"\\\\\"'`goal -> implementation structure'\"\\\\\"'` splitter.'\"\\\\n2. **Output.** It builds the \\\\\"'`Master Ledger'\"\\\\\"'`: domains, one test suite per spec, inputs, effects, helpers, screens/pages, components, state, control-flow entries, unresolved questions, and spec candidates.'\"\\\\n3. **Use.** Use it after stack analysis when the operator needs code execution order and concrete implementation structure.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## B. Boundary\\\\n\\\\n1. **No architecture invention.** It must speak with words present in the \\\\\"'`Specs'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Data Model'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Runtime State'\"\\\\\"'`, existing codebase, references, or operator instruction.'\"\\\\n2. **No one-pass inference.** It creates the \\\\\"'`Master Ledger'\"\\\\\"'` section by section, then re-assesses each section.'\"\\\\n3. **Gate.** It is ready for \\\\\"'`executor-implement'\"\\\\\"'` only when there are no dangling references, unreachable control-flow entries, missing helpers/effects/components/state/domains, or blocking unresolved items.'\"\\\\n\"'`);\nwriteCard('\"'card-skill-executor-implement', \"'`## A. Why Kept'\"\\\\n\\\\n1. **Best direct implementation skill.** \\\\\"'`executor-implement'\"\\\\\"'` consumes the '\"\\\\\"'`Master Ledger'\"\\\\\"'` and turns the generated scaffold into complete implementation.'\"\\\\n2. **Scope.** It delivers real code with no placeholder code, no missing feature, and no bug from the prepared scaffold.\\\\n3. **Use.** Use it after \\\\\"'`executor-spec'\"\\\\\"'`, not before.'\"\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## B. Boundary\\\\n\\\\n1. **No architecture inference.** It must use the \\\\\"'`Root Blocks'\"\\\\\"'`, domains, screens/pages, components, inputs, actions, controllers, helpers, effects, state, and tests from the '\"\\\\\"'`Master Ledger'\"\\\\\"'`.'\"\\\\n2. **Stop condition.** If implementation requires a missing \\\\\"'`Spec'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Data Model'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Runtime State'\"\\\\\"'`, domain, input, action, controller, helper, effect, screen/page, component, or test, stop and ask an operator question.'\"\\\\n3. **Verification.** Confirm each \\\\\"'`Master Ledger'\"\\\\\"'` item is implemented, each '\"\\\\\"'`Spec'\"\\\\\"'` still has a test suite, helper/effect unit tests pass, compile when applicable, launch app/site when applicable, screenshot every screen, and inspect the result.'\"\\\\n\"'`);\nwriteCard('\"'card-skill-ticket-solver', \"'`## A. Why Kept'\"\\\\n\\\\n1. **Best existing ticket implementer.** \\\\\"'`ticket-solver'\"\\\\\"'` solves an existing GitLab ticket end to end.'\"\\\\n2. **Planning before code.** It still creates a working document and full control-flow DAG before implementation.\\\\n3. **Use.** Use it after a ticket exists, not at the start of a broad goal.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## B. Boundary\\\\n\\\\n1. **Downstream role.** It should consume a prepared ticket, create the working DAG, implement, test, and report evidence.\\\\n2. **Not a broad splitter.** It should not replace \\\\\"'`executor-spec'\"\\\\\"'` for turning broad specs into implementation structure.'\"\\\\n3. **Best fit.** Use when the workflow state is already a GitLab issue and the requested outcome is a solved ticket.\\\\n\"'`);\nwriteCard('\"'card-skill-feature-analyzer', \"'`## A. Why Kept'\"\\\\n\\\\n1. **Best feature surface mapper.** \\\\\"'`feature/analyzer'\"\\\\\"'` maps feature intent to codebase surface area.'\"\\\\n2. **Output.** It produces evidence-backed task breakdown, risks, planner TODOs, planner decisions, and recommended implementation order.\\\\n3. **Use.** Use before \\\\\"'`feature/planner'\"\\\\\"'` when a feature needs grounded codebase surface mapping before the implementation DAG.'\"\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## B. Boundary\\\\n\\\\n1. **Feature issue scope.** It is useful when the unit of work is one feature issue.\\\\n2. **Not an implementer.** It prepares the planner; it does not implement code.\\\\n3. **No epic/product decomposition.** It is kept because it is closer to implementation order than \\\\\"'`product/decomposer'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`epic/decomposer'\"\\\\\"'`, or other composer roles.'\"\\\\n\"'`);\nwriteCard('\"'card-skill-feature-planner', \"'`## A. Why Kept'\"\\\\n\\\\n1. **Best single-feature implementation planner.** \\\\\"'`feature/planner'\"\\\\\"'` produces the implementation plan for one feature issue.'\"\\\\n2. **Output.** It creates \\\\\"'`Spec'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Codebase Impact Intent'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Dependency Blockers'\"\\\\\"'`, and '\"\\\\\"'`Ideal Control-flow DAG'\"\\\\\"'`.'\"\\\\n3. **Use.** Use it after \\\\\"'`feature/analyzer'\"\\\\\"'` when the needed output is a feature-level implementation DAG.'\"\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## B. Boundary\\\\n\\\\n1. **No child issues.** It does not create child issues.\\\\n2. **One feature.** It is for one feature issue, not a whole product or epic pipeline.\\\\n3. **Implementation handoff.** Its output should feed implementation, audit, and verification steps in the feature pipeline.\\\\n\"'`);\nconst sourceContent = `## A. Chosen Skill Cards'\"\\\\n\\\\n1. **\\\\\"'`executor-spec'\"\\\\\"'`.** Best implementation planner: turns approved '\"\\\\\"'`Specs'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Data Model'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Runtime State'\"\\\\\"'`, and stack analysis into the '\"\\\\\"'`Master Ledger'\"\\\\\"'`.'\"\\\\n2. **\\\\\"'`executor-implement'\"\\\\\"'`.** Best direct implementation skill: consumes the '\"\\\\\"'`Master Ledger'\"\\\\\"'` and implements the scaffold with tests and verification.'\"\\\\n3. **\\\\\"'`ticket-solver'\"\\\\\"'`.** Best existing-ticket implementer: solves a prepared GitLab ticket end to end after creating a working document and control-flow DAG.'\"\\\\n4. **\\\\\"'`feature/analyzer'\"\\\\\"'`.** Best feature surface mapper: produces evidence-backed task breakdown and recommended implementation order.'\"\\\\n5. **\\\\\"'`feature/planner'\"\\\\\"'`.** Best single-feature implementation planner: produces '\"\\\\\"'`Spec'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Codebase Impact Intent'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`Dependency Blockers'\"\\\\\"'`, and '\"\\\\\"'`Ideal Control-flow DAG'\"\\\\\"'`.'\"\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## B. What Was Removed\\\\n\\\\n1. **Removed broad inventory cards.** The previous 30-card split was too much to read and has been removed from the active \\\\\"'`skills'\"\\\\\"'` ledger.'\"\\\\n2. **Removed irrelevant roles.** \\\\\"'`product/*'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`epic/*'\"\\\\\"'`, '\"\\\\\"'`*decomposer'\"\\\\\"'`, issue improvers, inbox treatment, and OpenSpec support cards were removed from this card set because they are not the best implementation-skill shortlist.'\"\\\\n3. **No separate gap card.** The orchestration gap is not kept as a card because the operator asked for no more than five skill cards.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## C. Recommended Chain\\\\n\\\\n1. **Broad specs to implementation.** Use \\\\\"'`executor-spec -> executor-implement'\"\\\\\"'` after the necessary precheck and stack analysis exist.'\"\\\\n2. **Existing GitLab ticket.** Use \\\\\"'`ticket-solver'\"\\\\\"'` when there is already a prepared ticket.'\"\\\\n3. **Single feature issue.** Use \\\\\"'`feature/analyzer -> feature/planner'\"\\\\\"'` when the work needs codebase surface mapping and a feature-level implementation DAG.'\"\\\\n\"'`;\nfs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, '\"'.decision-os/cards/skills/card-c48369dc-1d97-4c6c-ab36-fd01d819d03a.md'), sourceContent, 'utf8');\nfs.writeFileSync(ledgerPath, \"'`${JSON.stringify(ledger, null, 2)}'\"\\\\n\"'`, '\"'utf8');\nconsole.log(\"'`kept=${Array.from(keepSkillIds).join('\"',')}\"'`);\nconsole.log(`removed=${removeSkillIds.length}`);\nNODE'","aggregated_output":"","exit_code":null,"status":"in_progress"}}

````text
## A. Chosen Skill Cards

1. **`executor-spec`.** Best implementation planner: turns approved `Specs`, `Data Model`, `Runtime State`, and stack analysis into the `Master Ledger`.
2. **`executor-implement`.** Best direct implementation skill: consumes the `Master Ledger` and implements the scaffold with tests and verification.
3. **`ticket-solver`.** Best existing-ticket implementer: solves a prepared GitLab ticket end to end after creating a working document and control-flow DAG.
4. **`feature/analyzer`.** Best feature surface mapper: produces evidence-backed task breakdown and recommended implementation order.
5. **`feature/planner`.** Best single-feature implementation planner: produces `Spec`, `Codebase Impact Intent`, `Dependency Blockers`, and `Ideal Control-flow DAG`.

---

## B. What Was Removed

1. **Removed broad inventory cards.** The previous 30-card split was too much to read and has been removed from the active `skills` ledger.
2. **Removed irrelevant roles.** `product/*`, `epic/*`, `*decomposer`, issue improvers, inbox treatment, and OpenSpec support cards were removed from this card set because they are not the best implementation-skill shortlist.
3. **No separate gap card.** The orchestration gap is not kept as a card because the operator asked for no more than five skill cards.

---

## C. Recommended Chain

1. **Broad specs to implementation.** Use `executor-spec -> executor-implement` after the necessary precheck and stack analysis exist.
2. **Existing GitLab ticket.** Use `ticket-solver` when there is already a prepared ticket.
3. **Single feature issue.** Use `feature/analyzer -> feature/planner` when the work needs codebase surface mapping and a feature-level implementation DAG.

---

## D. Ticket Skills Worth Remembering

1. **`ticket-solver`.** Keep this as one of the five cards because it is the implementation-facing ticket skill: it solves an existing GitLab ticket end to end with a working document, control-flow DAG, tests, and verification evidence.
2. **`openticket`.** Interesting, but not kept as a card in this shortlist because it creates a GitLab issue from a broad operator-reported problem; it is ticket intake, not implementation.
3. **`improveticket`.** Interesting, but not kept as a card in this shortlist because it rewrites an existing weak GitLab issue into OpenTicket structure and applies factory labels after approval; it is issue improvement, not implementation.
4. **`ticket/improver`.** Interesting, but not kept as a card in this shortlist because it is the DroidFactory issue normalizer for an `improve` issue; it prepares the pipeline, then implementation happens downstream.
````
